result.planSummary: Addressed latest blocking SV-03-01 by extending SQLite row-level turn/chunk merge behavior beyond token metadata: stale incoming rows that omit nested derived artifacts now preserve existing turn lower-band projections and chunk detailed/brief lower-band artifacts, while explicit incoming artifact records can still update status/text. Added verifier-shaped regression coverage for omitted nested artifacts and kept the prior token metadata preservation and no-op maintenance count coverage green. Targeted Story 3 tests and typecheck pass; `npm run verify-all` reached E2E and failed on a repeated PI setup-prompt timeout in the fixture command suite with empty stdout/stderr and no fetch log.

Switched bounded token maintenance to row-level writes, persisted maintenance run status, and changed background fixed counts to actual resolved maintenance debt instead of hard-coded phase counts.
Used row-level turn writes for smooth persistence when available.
Used row-level turn writes for lower-band projection persistence when available.
Used row-level chunk writes for chunk-state refreshes and refined transcript-change handling so semantic artifacts are not invalidated on no-op refreshes.
Used row-level chunk writes for semantic artifact persistence and queued async compression via an unref’d timer so short-lived PI runs can exit cleanly.
Persisted full manual-repair maintenance status after success/failure.
Added reusable SQLite maintenance fixture and fake exact-token counter helpers for Story 3 coverage.
Added bounded background maintenance, stale canonical write coverage, same-row token metadata preservation, omitted nested artifact preservation, and dependent chunk readiness regression coverage.
Added full manual repair success/failure coverage with persisted maintenance status assertions.
Added thread-level maintenance reporting coverage, bounded-vs-manual distinction, and already-clean background no-op fixed-count coverage.
Extended token tests to cover exact SQLite repair metadata persistence and partial-repair debt visibility.

gatesRun.command: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "^e2e: fixture creation command$|^/lh-fixture creates a valid thread-shaped fixture$" tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts

findingsFixed: SV-03-01: SQLite turn row writes now preserve an existing smooth.lowerBandProjection when a stale incoming same-row turn omits that nested artifact while updating another derived field.
SV-03-01: SQLite chunk row writes now preserve existing lowerBand.detailed and lowerBand.brief artifacts when a stale incoming same-row chunk omits lowerBand while updating another derived field.
Confirmed the prior SV-03-01 token metadata preservation still passes and adjusted the dependent chunk readiness regression to use an explicit pending projection update rather than artifact omission.
Confirmed SV-03-02 remains fixed: already-clean background maintenance reports fixedCount 0, skippedCount 0, failedCount 0, and remainingDebtCount 0.
findingsSurfaced: `npm run verify-all` failed in E2E after service tests passed 552/552 because the `/lh-fixture` setup prompt timed out with PI exit code 124; the preserved run log had empty stdout/stderr and no fetch log. A narrow rerun of the fixture E2E reproduced the same setup-prompt timeout.

openQuestions: Should the repeated PI setup-prompt timeout in `tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts` be treated as an external/runtime flake and rerun by verification, or should a separate follow-up triage that E2E command setup path outside Story 3 scope?
result.recommendedNextStep: Run verifier on the updated SV-03-01 artifact changes; separately rerun or triage the isolated PI fixture-command E2E timeout if the gate environment continues to time out before producing a fetch log.
